title: DNS Service Binding RFC 9461 Response Message Parser Architecture
purpose: Define the bounded RFC 9461 DNS response parser boundary for SVCB answers and Additional-section address records.
design_summary: `DnsServiceBindingResponseMessage` parses a complete DNS response envelope: header counts, question names, answer records, authority records, and Additional records. Answer-section SVCB records are dispatched to the existing AliasMode and ServiceMode parsers, preserving their stricter RFC 9460 TargetName and SvcParam validation. Additional-section Internet-class A and AAAA records are converted into scalar `DnsServiceBindingAdditionalAddress` values keyed by owner name, while unsupported records and non-Internet address records are skipped.
data_and_state_considerations: The parser is a pure byte-to-value helper over a single DNS message. It does not perform DNS queries, validate DNSSEC signatures, choose resolver policy, install host resolver configuration, publish operator DNS records, or establish encrypted DNS transports.
edge_cases_and_constraints: DNS owner names can use RFC 1035 compression; SVCB RDATA TargetName values still use the existing uncompressed parser.
Compression pointers are bounded and cyclic or out-of-message pointers are rejected.
SVCB RDATA shorter than SvcPriority is rejected before dispatch.
Additional-section A and AAAA records must have exactly four and sixteen address octets respectively.
Trailing bytes after the declared DNS sections are rejected.
risks: The parser does not authenticate DNS response data.
The parser does not rank addresses or merge them into endpoint connection policy.
The parser does not implement a recursive or stub resolver.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: Keeping response parsing in `Incursa.Quic.Dns` provides a reusable scalar input for future discovery adapters while avoiding coupling to QUIC transport runtime, platform resolver APIs, or DNSSEC policy.
